To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a new transform, based on the wavelet concept and called the wavelet transform, is proposed to represent signals in the time-frequency plane; (2) this transform, which is a generalization of the discrete Fourier transform, has the advantage of being invertible; (3) the transform is defined in a very simple way; and (4) it is possible to use it for time-frequency digital filtering of finite signals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new method to analyze and to filter digital signals of short duration by means of time-frequency representations.
we have developed a new transform, which we call the discrete wavelet transform (DWT).
we have shown that a time-frequency representation based on a discrete wavelet transform is invertible and that it can be used for the time-frequency filtering of digital signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method is very efficient in terms of computation and memory requirements.
the wavelet concept can be used to define a purely invertible transform, which allows us to represent signals in the time-frequency domains as easily as in the conventional frequency domain.
we have shown that it is possible to use a time-frequency representation of a finite signal in the time or frequency domains.
